title: Harbour Gate Clearing in five minutes

steps.title: Where the work stands
steps.body: {{summary:Open jobs}} open jobs, {{summary:At risk}} at risk of demurrage and {{summary:To be invoiced}} waiting to be invoiced. Read straight from the records, never typed in.

steps.title: Every job, by stage
steps.body: Jobs sit in the stage they have reached, and the money is added up per stage: {{group:Assessed}}.

steps.title: The demurrage clock
steps.body: Once a container is past its free days it starts costing money. The red chip says which jobs are costing you now.

steps.title: A job knows its next step
steps.body: The path is ten stages long, and Clicker offers only the step your role may take. Anyone else sees whose move it is.

steps.title: Costs paid on the client's behalf
steps.body: Each one is approved by Accounts before it can be billed, and whoever recorded it can't approve it.

steps.title: Gate-out drafts the invoice
steps.body: One click, and Clicker drafts the client's invoice from the service fee and every approved cost. Try it, or press Next to carry on.

steps.title: Nobody typed that invoice
steps.body: The trail says who moved the job, and that Clicker drafted the invoice itself. Anything not yet approved is named in its notes.

steps.title: See it as someone else
steps.body: Choose View as role to see exactly what a Field agent sees. Their jobs only, no money. The same rules the server enforces.

steps.title: Who can do what
steps.body: Roles live on the Team page, and changing one changes what that person sees the next time they open a screen.

ending: What Clicker did that you did not have to: sum every stage, count every free day, draft the invoice, and keep each person to what their role allows.
